title: Pixelproof adapter registration v1
description: How a project declares adapters that are not bundled with Pixelproof. Bundled adapters need no entry here: they are trusted and discovered from the repository (ADR 0004). Anything registered through this file runs out of process.

id.description: Must be unique across all adapters of its kind. Duplicate ids are a hard error rather than a last-one-wins race.

command.description: Executable path or bare name resolved on PATH. Never passed to a shell: it is argv[0], so no quoting or metacharacter interpretation applies.

args.description: Fixed leading arguments. The protocol request itself arrives on stdin, not as an argument.

trust.description: Only `external` is accepted here. In-process trust is not grantable by configuration, because a config file that could grant it would be an arbitrary-code-execution vector (ADR 0004).

timeoutMs.description: Deadline for a single operation. On expiry the whole process tree is terminated, not just the direct child.

env.description: Allowlist of environment variable names to forward. The adapter otherwise receives a minimal environment; secrets are not passed implicitly.

capabilities.description: Optional static declaration used only when the adapter does not answer the `describe` handshake. The handshake is the primary mechanism; this exists so a trivial script need not implement it.
